Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment uses chemical proteomics (affinity pull-downs) followed by DDA and LFQ. While the study focuses on methyltransferases, the MS analysis itself is a standard bottom-up LFQ approach to identify captured proteins, not a PTM-enrichment workflow for the methyl marks themselves (which were analyzed via Western Blot).

scope: Amine derivatized compounds were coupled to NHS-activated Sepharose 4 fast flow beads (GE Healthcare).
Biotin derivatized compounds were coupled to UltraLink Immobilized Streptavidin Plus beads (GE Healthcare).
Derivatised beads were then washed with DMSO (3 × 500 μL), Buffer A (3 × 1 mL), and incubated with cell lysates (2 mg of protein per pulldown, at 6 mg mL−1)

Beads and treated lysates were incubated for 2 h at 4 °C, before being washed with Buffer A (5 mL), Buffer B (50 mM HEPES pH 7.5, 100 mM NaCl, 500 μM EDTA, 2.5 mL), and eluted with formic acid (100 mM, 250 μL).
The EED and Type I PRMT affinity reagents specifically enriched their cognate targets from cell lysates as demonstrated by immunoblotting (Supplementary Fig. 1).

Profiling of the pan Type I PRMT inhibitor MS023 in HEK293 cell lysates using label-free quantification (LFQ) protein mass spectrometry showed engagement of several PRMTs including PRMT1, 3, 4, and 6 and their respective binding partners
